NVDA.rationale: NVIDIA exhibits exceptional fundamental health and trajectory: Q1 FY27 revenue of $81.6B (+85% YoY), EPS of $2.39 (+215% YoY), gross margins of 75%, operating cash flow of $50.3B, and a fortress balance sheet with only $8.5B debt against $195B equity. The company holds ~86% AI GPU market share and is expanding into CPUs (Vera platform) and networking (now #1 in data center Ethernet switching). Valuation is attractive vs. own history: P/E of 32.2x sits at the bottom of its 30.6-66.8x 12-month range, having compressed from 56x+ in April/May as earnings surged. Forward P/E of ~23x on $91B Q2 guidance is compelling for 85%+ growth. However, several factors temper the score: (1) extreme revenue concentration with ~90% from data center and ~50% from five hyperscaler customers who are developing competing custom chips (Google TPUs, Amazon Trainium, Microsoft Maia); (2) regulatory overhang from Senator Warren's export control investigation and China chip smuggling allegations; (3) macro headwinds including 4.2% inflation rising 10Y yields at 4.46%; (4) the SpaceX IPO rotation creating near-term capital flow pressure away from AI names. The June 24 shareholder meeting provides a modest near-term catalyst for positive commentary on Vera CPU launch and capital return program, but is unlikely to be a major re-rating event. The $80B buyback authorization and 25x dividend increase signal management confidence and provide valuation support.
